html:
The Burana Tower is a brick minaret in the Chuy valley of Kyrgyzstan, built in about the 11th century at Balasagun, a capital of the Kara-Khanid Khanate.

The Kara-Khanids were the first Turkic dynasty to take up Islam, and Balasagun was one of their great cities. The scholar Yusuf Balasaguni, born there, wrote the Kutadgu Bilig, an early long poem in Turkic. In the 12th century the city fell to the Kara Khitai, and after the Mongols it was slowly abandoned.

Earthquakes over the centuries brought down the top of the tower, which once stood about twice its present height; it was partly restored in the 1970s. Around it lie the ruins of the town and a field of balbals, carved stone figures from older Turkic graves. The site is part of the Silk Roads World Heritage listing.
sum: The Burana Tower is a brick minaret in the Chuy valley of Kyrgyzstan, built in about the 11th century at Balasagun, a capital of the Kara-Khanid Khanate.
